transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The 2026 midterm elections are on track
to be the most expensive on record.
According to the latest campaign finance filings,
Democratic candidates and Elon Musk
dominated the last fundraising period.
NPR's Stephen Fowler has more.
Musk added more than a quarter billion dollars
in new contributions to Republican politics,
including more than 150 million to a super PAC
aimed at the Texas Senate race.
That's more than Republican Ken Paxton
and Democrat James Tallarico have raised
combined the entire midterm cycle.
Speaking of Tallarico, his record-setting third quarter,
60 plus million dollar haul leads the way
for Democratic Senate nominees,
who vastly outraised their opponents
in four out of every five cases.
If you just look at the 13 races
that cook political report rates as competitive,
Republicans are being outraised
by at least a five to one margin.
That, and how the parties are spending money,
suggests both parties are preparing
for a potential blue wave.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
People in the Canadian province of Alberta
are voting today on a referendum question.
It could change Canada's political landscape.
There are 10 questions on the ballot.
Dan Karpenchuk reports the most important
is whether the province will stay in Canada.
Even if Albertans vote to stay in Canada,
the pro-separative side says the frustration
will likely remain for years to come.
A vote in favor of separation would trigger
another referendum, this one binding,
that would lead to the process of Alberta leaving Canada.
Those in favor of staying,
including Prime Minister Mark Carney,
who is from Alberta, have pulled out all the stops
in recent weeks to get the message across
that Alberta and Canada are stronger together.
Election officials say with 10 separate ballots each,
people should be prepared for long lineups
at polling stations.
All ballots must be counted by hand,
with the results taking at least 48 hours.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenchuk in Toronto.
Israeli police say they've arrested at least 10 suspects
that follows Israeli settler attacks
on a Washington Post photographer and European diplomats.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports from Tel Aviv.
Israeli police released footage
of their arrests this morning.
The footage appears to show young settlers
apprehended from unauthorized settlement outposts
in the West Bank.
These arrests are rare, as settler violence has expanded
under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government,
with a strategy of claiming more land for Israel.
US Ambassador Mike Huckabee praised the arrests.
He said the attack on Heidi Levine,
the Washington Post journalist,
was a despicable act of terror.
An Israeli group tracking Israeli settler
and soldier violence has counted more than 500 violent
incidents across more than 180 Palestinian communities
in just the last three weeks.
More attacks were reported today.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
You're listening to NPR.
President Trump has endorsed
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election.
He is citing Netanyahu's support
for the ongoing war against Iran.
President Trump says his planned renovations
to a Washington, D.C. golf course will begin immediately.
Writing online this morning, Trump dismissed opponents
who have filed a lawsuit to stop him.
A federal judge has ordered a halt to any renovation work
while the lawsuit is heard.
Trump called the judge, quote, "a crazed lunatic."
Trump says the Interior Department is going ahead
with the work on the course
because they don't need an approval.
It's not clear that's true.
Hollywood just had a surprisingly strong weekend
and Pierre's Bob Mondello reports
the emphasis is definitely on the surprise.
The number one film this weekend
was the martial arts action flick "Street Fighter,"
but it's the number two film that's causing a stir.
You really feel you did nothing wrong.
I did not.
In "You Can See Everything,"
Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes,
who's currently serving a prison sentence
for defrauding investors,
is interrogated by absurdist comedian Nathan Fielder.
Does any part of you worry about me being here 24/7?
I don't think so.
Well, what if I see something that makes you look bad?
Produced in secret, the almost three-hour movie
was on no one's radar until two months ago.
Then a scene from it went viral,
as did talk of a mid-film surprise.
And this weekend, with spoiler-reverse crowds
flocking to fewer than 1,000 theaters,
you can see "Everything"
posted the second best opening ever for a documentary.
Not surprisingly, the film will expand its run next week.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Elon Musk and Democratic candidates dominate record-setting 2026 midterm campaign fundraising
Alberta voters cast ballots in ten-question referendum, including whether to stay in Canada
Israeli police arrest at least 10 settlers after attacks on Washington Post photographer and diplomats
Trump endorses Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election, citing support for war against Iran
Trump says Washington D.C. golf course renovations will proceed despite judge's halt order
Nathan Fielder's documentary 'You Can See Everything' with Elizabeth Holmes posts strong weekend opening
